writes.rule: Per subtopic seen: pMastery 0.7 if right at D2/D3, 0.55 if right at D1, 0.25 if wrong; level L0-L3 from the ladder step reached
Prerequisite-gap index = 100 x weighted misses / weighted items seen in slots 1-4, averaged over groups
Groups with the highest Part A percent (top 1-2, only if >= 65%)
Groups with the lowest Part A percent (bottom 1-2, only if < 65%)
Calibration = 1 - mean |confidence/5 - correct| over Part A (feeds the first MCI reading)
Highest difficulty answered correctly twice in a row: D1 low, D2 medium, D3 high
Verbal reasoning = percent of Part B verbal items right
Numerical reasoning = percent of Part B numerical items right
Abstract reasoning = percent of Part B abstract items right
Spatial reasoning = percent of Part B spatial items right
Logical deduction = percent right on Part B items tagged p65
Numeracy fluency = numerical percent scaled by speed (right answers under target time count 1.2x, max 100)
Processing speed = 100 x share of Part B items answered right within target seconds
RIASEC profile: each career-interest item scored 1-5; letter score = mean of its 2 items; top 3 letters form the code (e.g. IRC)

items.stem: Solve 5x - 7 = 3x + 9.
items.subtopicHint: Linear equations with unknowns on both sides

items.stem: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides 6 cm and 8 cm. How long is the hypotenuse?
A 13 m ladder leans against a wall with its foot 5 m from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
Simplify 4a + 3b - a + 2b.
items.markingKey: D. 3a + 5b. Collect like terms

items.stem: Expand (a + b)².
items.markingKey: B. a² + 2ab + b². (a + b)(a + b) = a² + ab + ab + b²

items.stem: Use an identity to work out 102 x 98.
Write 3/5 as a percentage.
A price rises from 12 000 to 13 800. What is the percentage increase?
After a 25% discount a book costs 450. What was the original price?
items.markingKey: B. 600. 450 is 75% of the original, and 450 ÷ 0.75 = 600

items.stem: Simplify √12.
Simplify √18 + √8.
Rationalise the denominator of 6/√3.
Evaluate 8^(1/3).
items.markingKey: B. 2. The cube root of 8

items.stem: Simplify (x⁶)^(1/2).
items.markingKey: A. x³. Multiply the exponents

items.stem: Factorise x² + 5x + 6.
Factorise x² - x - 12.
Factorise 2x² + 7x + 3.
Solve x + y = 10 and x - y = 2.
Solve 2x + y = 7 and x + y = 4.
items.markingKey: B. x = 3, y = 1. Subtract: x = 3

items.stem: Two cinema tickets and three snacks cost 31; one ticket and two snacks cost 17. How much is one ticket?
items.markingKey: A. 11. 2t + 3s = 31 and t + 2s = 17 give s = 3, t = 11

items.stem: Why does the smell of perfume spread across a still room?
items.answer: Its particles diffuse, moving randomly from high to low concentration
options: Air pushes the perfume in one direction
Its particles diffuse, moving randomly from high to low concentration
Perfume is lighter than air, so it only rises
items.markingKey: C. Its particles diffuse, moving randomly from high to low concentration. Random particle motion spreads the perfume out

items.stem: Which of these is a compound?
items.markingKey: A. water. Water is hydrogen and oxygen chemically joined; air is a mixture

items.stem: Which statement about a mixture of iron filings and sulfur powder is true?
items.answer: The iron can be separated with a magnet
options: The iron can be separated with a magnet
items.markingKey: C. The iron can be separated with a magnet. In a mixture each substance keeps its own properties

items.stem: Pressure is
items.subtopicHint: Pressure as force per unit area
items.markingKey: B. force per unit area. p = F / A

items.stem: Why is it easier to cut with a sharp knife than a blunt one?
items.answer: The sharp edge has a smaller area, so the same force gives more pressure
items.subtopicHint: Pressure as force per unit area
options: Blunt knives only have more friction
Sharp knives push with more force by themselves
The sharp edge has a smaller area, so the same force gives more pressure
items.markingKey: D. The sharp edge has a smaller area, so the same force gives more pressure. Smaller area, larger pressure

items.stem: A box weighing 600 N rests on a base of area 0.5 m². What pressure does it exert on the floor?
items.subtopicHint: Pressure as force per unit area

items.stem: Which part of a cell controls its activities?
items.subtopicHint: Cell structure: plant and animal cells
items.markingKey: D. nucleus. The nucleus holds the genetic instructions

items.stem: Onion peel cells and cheek cells are viewed under a microscope. Which difference will you see?
items.answer: Onion cells have a cell wall and a regular shape; cheek cells do not
items.subtopicHint: Cell structure: plant and animal cells
options: Cheek cells have a large central vacuole
Onion cells have a cell wall and a regular shape; cheek cells do not
items.markingKey: D. Onion cells have a cell wall and a regular shape; cheek cells do not. Only plant cells have cell walls

items.stem: A cell placed in pure water swells but does not burst. Which cell is it most likely to be?
items.answer: A plant cell, because its cell wall resists bursting
items.subtopicHint: Cell structure: plant and animal cells
options: A plant cell, because its cell wall resists bursting
Any cell, since water never enters cells
An animal cell, because it has a cell membrane
items.markingKey: A. A plant cell, because its cell wall resists bursting. Animal cells without a wall can burst in pure water

items.stem: Mitosis produces
items.markingKey: C. two genetically identical cells. Mitosis is for growth and repair

items.stem: Explain why mitosis is important when you cut your skin.
items.answer: It produces new identical cells to repair the tissue
options: It produces new identical cells to repair the tissue
items.markingKey: B. It produces new identical cells to repair the tissue. New cells replace damaged ones

items.stem: A human body cell has 46 chromosomes. How many are in each cell produced by mitosis, and by meiosis?
items.markingKey: D. 46 after mitosis, 23 after meiosis. Meiosis halves the chromosome number for gametes

items.stem: An allele that shows its effect whenever it is present is
items.markingKey: B. dominant. A dominant allele is expressed in heterozygotes

items.stem: Two Tt pea plants are crossed (T = tall, dominant). What fraction of the offspring is expected to be short?
items.markingKey: B. 1/4. Only tt plants are short: 1 in 4

items.stem: A brown-eyed parent (Bb) and a blue-eyed parent (bb) have a child. What is the probability that the child has blue eyes?
items.markingKey: D. 50%. Bb x bb gives Bb and bb in equal numbers

items.stem: The small gap between two neurones is called a
items.subtopicHint: The nervous system and reflex arcs
items.markingKey: C. synapse. Chemicals cross the synapse to pass on the impulse

items.stem: What is the correct order of a reflex arc?
items.answer: receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → effector
items.subtopicHint: The nervous system and reflex arcs
options: effector → motor neurone → relay neurone → sensory neurone → receptor
receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → effector
receptor → motor neurone → relay neurone → sensory neurone → effector
items.markingKey: B. receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → effector. Stimulus in, response out

items.stem: Explain why reflex actions are faster than voluntary actions.
items.answer: The impulse passes through the spinal cord without needing a conscious decision in the brain
items.subtopicHint: The nervous system and reflex arcs
options: The impulse passes through the spinal cord without needing a conscious decision in the brain
items.markingKey: D. The impulse passes through the spinal cord without needing a conscious decision in the brain. A shorter pathway saves time

items.stem: What is the maximum number of electrons in the first shell?
items.markingKey: A. 2. The first shell holds 2

items.stem: What is the electron arrangement of sodium (atomic number 11)?
Explain why Group 1 metals are very reactive.
items.answer: They lose their single outer electron easily to get a stable arrangement
options: They lose their single outer electron easily to get a stable arrangement
items.markingKey: C. They lose their single outer electron easily to get a stable arrangement. One electron to lose

items.stem: The ground is wet and people are carrying umbrellas. It ___ have rained.
items.markingKey: C. must. 'Must have' expresses a confident deduction

items.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly as direct speech?
items.markingKey: B. "Close the window," said Mother.. Only the spoken words go inside the quotation marks, followed by a comma

items.stem: Change to indirect speech: She said, 'I will call you tomorrow.'
items.answer: She said that she would call me the next day.
options: She said she will called me tomorrow.
She said that she would call me the next day.
She told that she would calls me the next day.
She said that I will call you tomorrow.
items.markingKey: B. She said that she would call me the next day.. 'Will' becomes 'would', 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'

items.stem: Which is the best title for a paragraph about saving water by fixing leaks, using buckets and reusing water?
items.markingKey: A. Simple Ways to Save Water. A title should cover the main idea of the whole paragraph

items.stem: Read: "Mangroves grow along tropical coasts. Their tangled roots hold soil in place, slow down storm waves and shelter young fish. Many mangrove forests are being cleared for farms and buildings." Which summary is best?
items.answer: Mangroves protect coasts and wildlife but are being cleared
options: Farms are more important than mangroves
Mangroves protect coasts and wildlife but are being cleared
items.markingKey: D. Mangroves protect coasts and wildlife but are being cleared. A summary keeps the main points and leaves out detail

items.stem: Which sentence would NOT belong in a summary of a text explaining how vaccines work?
items.answer: My cousin was scared of injections when he was little.
options: My cousin was scared of injections when he was little.
Vaccines train the immune system to recognise germs.
This prepares the body to fight infection quickly.
items.markingKey: A. My cousin was scared of injections when he was little.. Personal anecdotes are not main points

items.stem: 'Silent sea, softly sighing' mainly uses
items.markingKey: C. alliteration. The repeated 's' sound

items.stem: 'I have told you a million times!' is an example of
items.markingKey: D. hyperbole. Deliberate exaggeration for effect

items.stem: What is the effect of the simile in 'Her words were as sharp as broken glass'?
items.answer: It shows her words were hurtful
options: It shows her words were hurtful
items.markingKey: D. It shows her words were hurtful. Broken glass cuts, so the words wounded

items.stem: Which setting is most typical of Gothic fiction?
items.markingKey: D. A crumbling castle at night. Gothic settings are isolated, decaying and dark

items.stem: Why do Gothic writers often use storms and darkness?
items.answer: To build fear and reflect characters' inner turmoil
options: To build fear and reflect characters' inner turmoil
items.markingKey: A. To build fear and reflect characters' inner turmoil. Pathetic fallacy mirrors emotion

items.stem: 'The portrait's eyes seemed to follow her, though she knew it was only paint.' Analyse how the uncanny is created.
items.answer: Something familiar becomes unsettling, leaving the reader unsure what is real
options: Something familiar becomes unsettling, leaving the reader unsure what is real
The character is an art expert
The painting is described in technical detail
items.markingKey: A. Something familiar becomes unsettling, leaving the reader unsure what is real. The uncanny blends the ordinary and the strange

items.stem: In a tense scene, a run of short sentences usually
items.subtopicHint: Creating tension through sentence structure and pacing
items.markingKey: A. speeds up the pace. Short sentences read quickly

items.stem: Why might a writer place one very short sentence straight after a long, flowing one?
items.answer: To build up and then jolt the reader with a sudden change
items.subtopicHint: Creating tension through sentence structure and pacing
options: To build up and then jolt the reader with a sudden change
items.markingKey: B. To build up and then jolt the reader with a sudden change. Contrast creates impact

items.stem: 'She waited. And waited. Then, from somewhere below, a knock.' Analyse the effect of the fragments.
items.answer: They build suspense, making the reader pause on each moment before the knock
items.subtopicHint: Creating tension through sentence structure and pacing
options: They build suspense, making the reader pause on each moment before the knock
items.markingKey: C. They build suspense, making the reader pause on each moment before the knock. Fragments isolate moments and delay the reveal

items.stem: Propaganda is
items.answer: information used to promote a particular cause or view, often one-sided
items.subtopicHint: Propaganda versus protest: perspectives on war
options: information used to promote a particular cause or view, often one-sided
items.markingKey: C. information used to promote a particular cause or view, often one-sided. Propaganda persuades rather than informs

items.stem: A 1914 recruitment poster shows smiling soldiers and the words 'Your country needs YOU'. What is its purpose?
items.answer: To persuade men to join the army
items.subtopicHint: Propaganda versus protest: perspectives on war
options: To persuade men to join the army
To warn about the horrors of war
items.markingKey: A. To persuade men to join the army. Direct address and positive images persuade

items.stem: How might a soldier-poet's view of war differ from that poster's, and why?
items.answer: More bitter and realistic, because the poet experienced the suffering first-hand
items.subtopicHint: Propaganda versus protest: perspectives on war
options: Exactly the same, since both were official
More bitter and realistic, because the poet experienced the suffering first-hand
items.markingKey: B. More bitter and realistic, because the poet experienced the suffering first-hand. Perspective is shaped by experience and purpose

items.stem: In literature, a symbol is
items.answer: an object or image that represents a bigger idea
options: an object or image that represents a bigger idea
items.markingKey: C. an object or image that represents a bigger idea. Symbols carry meaning beyond the literal

items.stem: In many stories, a locked door is used to symbolise
items.answer: a barrier, a secret or a lost opportunity
options: a barrier, a secret or a lost opportunity
items.markingKey: A. a barrier, a secret or a lost opportunity. Doors suggest access and denial

items.stem: A novel mentions a caged bird every time the protagonist feels trapped. Analyse this motif.
items.answer: The caged bird mirrors the protagonist's lack of freedom and reinforces the theme
options: The caged bird mirrors the protagonist's lack of freedom and reinforces the theme
items.markingKey: D. The caged bird mirrors the protagonist's lack of freedom and reinforces the theme. Repetition signals significance

items.stem: Which was a cause of the Industrial Revolution in Britain?
items.answer: Plentiful coal and iron, and capital to invest
options: Plentiful coal and iron, and capital to invest
items.markingKey: D. Plentiful coal and iron, and capital to invest. Resources plus investment

items.stem: The Columbian Exchange refers to
items.answer: the transfer of plants, animals and diseases between the Americas and Europe, Africa and Asia after 1492
options: the transfer of plants, animals and diseases between the Americas and Europe, Africa and Asia after 1492
items.markingKey: D. the transfer of plants, animals and diseases between the Americas and Europe, Africa and Asia after 1492. Named after Columbus's voyages

items.stem: Which crop was carried from the Americas to Europe and Asia in the Columbian Exchange?
items.markingKey: D. potato. Potatoes, maize and tomatoes came from the Americas

items.stem: In a democracy, laws are made by
items.subtopicHint: Rules, laws and types of government
items.markingKey: D. elected representatives. Representatives are accountable to voters

items.stem: Why do societies need laws?
items.answer: To protect rights and settle disputes fairly
items.subtopicHint: Rules, laws and types of government
options: To protect rights and settle disputes fairly
items.markingKey: A. To protect rights and settle disputes fairly. Laws create order and fairness

items.stem: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child includes the right to education. Who has the main duty to make sure this right is met?
items.subtopicHint: Rules, laws and types of government
items.markingKey: C. Governments. States that ratify the convention are duty-bearers

items.stem: Scarcity means that
items.answer: wants are unlimited but resources are limited
options: there is too much of everything
wants are unlimited but resources are limited
items.markingKey: C. wants are unlimited but resources are limited. The basic economic problem

items.stem: Opportunity cost is
items.answer: the next best alternative given up
options: the total cost of all choices
the next best alternative given up
items.markingKey: B. the next best alternative given up. Every choice has a cost in what you give up

items.stem: A student goes to a concert instead of working a paid shift worth 40. What is the opportunity cost?
items.answer: The 40 she could have earned from the shift
options: The 40 she could have earned from the shift
items.markingKey: A. The 40 she could have earned from the shift. The forgone income is the next best alternative

items.stem: Before 1789, French society was divided into three
items.markingKey: A. Estates. Clergy, nobility and everyone else

items.stem: Which was a key cause of the French Revolution?
items.answer: A financial crisis and unfair taxes that fell mostly on the Third Estate
options: A financial crisis and unfair taxes that fell mostly on the Third Estate
items.markingKey: A. A financial crisis and unfair taxes that fell mostly on the Third Estate. Debt and inequality combined

items.stem: How did Enlightenment ideas contribute to the Revolution?
items.answer: They challenged the divine right of kings and promoted equality and rights
options: They challenged the divine right of kings and promoted equality and rights
items.markingKey: C. They challenged the divine right of kings and promoted equality and rights. Thinkers such as Rousseau questioned authority

items.stem: 'No taxation without representation' was a slogan of
items.markingKey: A. American colonists protesting British taxes. The colonists had no MPs in Parliament

items.stem: The Boston Tea Party (1773) was a protest against
items.markingKey: C. British taxes on tea. Colonists dumped tea into Boston Harbour

items.stem: Explain how the Seven Years' War helped cause the American Revolution.
items.answer: Britain's war debts led it to impose new taxes on the colonies
options: Britain's war debts led it to impose new taxes on the colonies
items.markingKey: A. Britain's war debts led it to impose new taxes on the colonies. The Stamp Act followed in 1765

items.stem: Nationalism is
items.answer: a strong sense of identity with, and loyalty to, one's nation
options: a strong sense of identity with, and loyalty to, one's nation
items.markingKey: D. a strong sense of identity with, and loyalty to, one's nation. Shared language, history and symbols build it

items.stem: Who led the unification of Germany, completed in 1871?
items.markingKey: B. Otto von Bismarck. Garibaldi and Mazzini were Italian nationalists

items.stem: How can nationalism both unite and divide people?
items.answer: It can unite those who share an identity but exclude or create conflict with others
options: It can unite those who share an identity but exclude or create conflict with others
items.markingKey: A. It can unite those who share an identity but exclude or create conflict with others. Balanced judgement needs both sides

items.stem: Which of these is a push factor in a rural area?
items.subtopicHint: Push and pull factors of rural-urban migration
items.markingKey: B. Lack of jobs. Push factors are reasons to leave

items.stem: Why are many megacities growing fastest in lower-income countries today?
items.answer: High rural-urban migration combined with natural increase
items.subtopicHint: Push and pull factors of rural-urban migration
options: High rural-urban migration combined with natural increase
items.markingKey: B. High rural-urban migration combined with natural increase. Both migration and births add people

items.stem: Evaluate the effects of rural-urban migration on a city.
items.answer: More workers for industry and services, but pressure on housing and services
items.subtopicHint: Push and pull factors of rural-urban migration
options: More workers for industry and services, but pressure on housing and services
items.markingKey: A. More workers for industry and services, but pressure on housing and services. Evaluation weighs both sides

items.stem: An arrow turns 90° clockwise at each step. Step 1 points up, step 2 right, step 3 down. Which way does it point at step 6?
items.explanation: The cycle repeats every 4 steps; step 6 = step 2

items.explanation: This is one of the 11 nets of a cube

items.explanation: A mirror swaps left and right: 3 becomes 9
